text:
The Rangers needed barely half a period to make this look easy. They led 3-0 before the first period was out and 4-0 midway through the second, and that cushion was just enough to survive a Seattle rally that ran the whole third period. New York held on, 4-3, for its third straight win.

The early gap was real. In the first period we had the Rangers well ahead on expected goals (a measure of chance quality), 2.39 to 0.93. Gabe Perreault scored 1:35 in, Tye Kartye tipped one in on the power play, and Jaroslav Chmelar added a third. Alexis Lafrenière, the No. 1 pick in 2020 out of Rimouski, was on the ice for all of it and finished with two assists, as did Mika Zibanejad. Pavel Dorofeyev's backhand in the second made it 4-0.

Then the game flipped. Seattle out-chanced New York 1.52 to 1.11 in the third, and Kaapo Kakko, a No. 2 pick by the Rangers in 2019 who now plays for Seattle, started the comeback 1:50 in. Jordan Eberle scored on the power play, and Vince Dunn's slap shot made it 4-3 with just under five minutes left, though the data gave it only a 5% chance of going in. Over the full game, our numbers gave the Rangers a 64% chance of deserving the win. Seattle also lost the faceoff battle, 32 to 21, and was hit twice as often, 36 to 18. Philipp Grubauer stopped 15 of 16 after Joey Daccord allowed three goals on 10 shots. The Rangers extend their winning streak to three, while Seattle has little to show for its late push.
